script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. APARTMENT - NIGHT

We open on JASON, 35, sitting alone in the dark. He's a successful businessman, but his face reveals deep unhappiness. He stares at a photo of him and his family.

JASON
(whispering)
Is this who I am?

Jason's phone rings. He checks the call ID. It's his former best friend, MARK.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

EXT. STREET - DAY

Jason walks to the coffee shop where he meets Mark, 36, looking worn and disheveled. They sit down, and Mark puts a photo on the table. It's of them as kids, laughing together.

MARK
Do you remember this?

Jason looks down, trying to recall the memory.

JASON
Yes, but that was a long time ago.

MARK
We promised each other that we'd always be there for each other. You were my brother, Jason.

Jason hesitates, looking uncomfortable.

JASON
I've built a life for myself, Mark. I can't just abandon it all and start over.

MARK
But is this the life you truly want? I've made mistakes, but I found mine. I found my passion, my identity.

INT. JASON'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jason sits alone again, staring at the photo. He picks up his laptop and starts researching volunteer programs abroad.

INT. VOLUNTEER ORGANIZATION OFFICE - DAY

Jason meets with the director of a volunteer organization. She explains the programs they offer and the impact they make.

DIRECTOR
You'll be making a real difference in people's lives.

JASON
I want to make a difference. I need to.

INT. APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jason packs his bags, ready to leave everything behind and start anew. He looks at the photo one last time, then tears it in half.

INT. AIRPORT - DAY

Jason boards a plane, looking out the window as the city fades into the distance. He closes his eyes, a sense of peace washing over him.

FADE OUT.

THE END
